Convert an ape::phylo tree into a TreePPL tree

Source: R/data.R
tp_phylo_to_tpPhylo.Rd

Builds the nested list that TreePPL reads as a binary tree:

Usage

tp_phylo_to_tpPhylo(
  phy,
  leaf_ctor = "Leaf",
  node_ctor = "Node",
  leaf_extra = function(i) list(),
  node_extra = function(i) list()
)

Arguments

phy

A rooted, binary tree of class phylo with branch lengths.

leaf_ctor

Constructor name used for tips, e.g. "Leaf" or "QTLeaf".

node_ctor

Constructor name used for internal nodes, e.g. "Node" or "QTNode".

leaf_extra

A function of one tip number returning a named list of extra leaf fields.

node_extra

A function of one internal node number returning a named list of extra node fields.

Value

A nested list of class tpPhylo, ready for tp_data() and tp_write_tppl_json(). The tip labels of phy are kept in the attribute "tip.label", in ape's tip order; they are not written to JSON. See print.tpPhylo() for the console output.

Details

{"__constructor__": "Node", "__data__": {"left": .., "right": .., "age": 4}}
{"__constructor__": "Leaf", "__data__": {"age": 0}}

Ages are times before the present: tips of an ultrametric tree get age 0 and the root gets the tree height. A node's left and right children are taken in the order they appear in phy$edge.

Extra fields, such as a leaf index or a node label, are added with leaf_extra and node_extra. Each receives the ape node number (tips are 1:ape::Ntip(phy), the root is ape::Ntip(phy) + 1) and must return a named list.

Examples

phy <- ape::read.tree(text = "((A:4,B:4):6,(C:7,D:7):3);")

# ClockTree (diversification models)
tree <- tp_phylo_to_tpPhylo(phy)
tree
#> Phylogenetic tree of class <tpPhylo>, with 4 tips and 3 internal nodes.
#> 
#> Rooted; includes branch lengths; root age = 10

# TreeLabeled (host-repertoire models): a label on every leaf and node
tree_labeled <- tp_phylo_to_tpPhylo(
  phy,
  leaf_extra = function(i) list(label = i),
  node_extra = function(i) list(label = i)
)
